newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Soccer-France ready to take centre stage.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-France ready to take centre stage.

text.p: In case people had forgotten, FIFA was reminding everyone on Thursday that there actually is a World Cup before the one to be co-hosted by Japan and South Korea in 2002.

Ever since it was announced on May 31 that the two Asian nations would become the first to share the event, Japan and South Korea have hogged the headlines from France, which will stage the next World Cup in little over 18 months time.
With construction of the new stadia proceeding smoothly, no major organisational gliches, no scandals, on or off the field, the French have fallen victim of their own efficiency.

At the same time that the French were quietly going about their business, controversy was rife in Japan and South Korea as the two nations argued over how the 2002 World Cup would be divided and organised.

At meetings on Wednesday the rivals were once again the centre of attention as FIFA confirmed that the co-hosts had reached agreement on all the major issues, including which would host the opening game and final.
Now with that out of the way, FIFA, world soccer's governing body, would just like the fuss surrounding the 2002 finals to simply disappear -- for now.
FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said: "Normally, you do one World Cup at a time as far as promotion is concerned. But then this is an unusual situation."
And a difficult one for FIFA as it desperately attempts to muscle the spotlight away from Asia and on to France.

FIFA vice-president and chairman of the organising committee Lennart Johansson said: "I'm embarrassed about the fact that we have a World Cup in 1998 and there is more interest and more discussion about 2002.
"But now we are in agreement about Japan and Korea and we can fully concentrate on this event in France."
FIFA, however, has done nothing to help shift interest back on to the French event.

After announcing that Japan and Korea had reached final decisions on the staging of the 2002 World Cup, FIFA refused to say what those decisions were and it was left to leaks at a high level to say that Japan will host the final and South Korea the opening match in six years time.
Those decisions are expected to be ratified by the executive committee which meets in Barcelona on December 7.

In contrast, there was only brief discussion about the next World Cup in a routine meeting on Thursday . The organising committee confirmed that the draw for the finals will be staged in the renovated stadium in Marseille in December 1997.
If a lack of attention for the 1998 World Cup finals troubles FIFA, it does not bother Michel Platini, joint-head of the French organising committee.
The former French international midfielder is patiently waiting in the wings knowing his country's turn to take centre stage is soon to come.
For the moment, Platini says, the 1998 World Cup is getting the attention where it should -- on the field.
"People often talk about things when there are problems but not often when they are going well," he shrugged.
